holidays.name: National Peanut Brittle Day
holidays.description: A crunchy, sweet celebration of the hard candy made of caramelized sugar and roasted peanuts. Time to risk your dental work for a good cause!
holidays.origin: Part of the American tradition of unofficial national food days, promoted by candy lovers and food-day calendars. Peanut brittle itself is a Southern classic, said to have been invented in the 1800s when a cook accidentally added baking soda to a candy batch.
holidays.funFact: Peanut brittle is often said to have been born from a kitchen mistake, and its signature airy crunch comes from baking soda reacting with hot sugar syrup to create tiny bubbles.

holidays.name: National Spouse's Day
holidays.description: A day set aside to appreciate your husband, wife, or life partner, ideally with more effort than remembering to take out the trash.
holidays.origin: Celebrated in the United States on January 26 as an unofficial observance encouraging people to show appreciation for their spouses, and often listed among national days in popular calendars.
holidays.funFact: It falls just a few weeks before Valentine's Day, making it the perfect low-pressure warm-up round for romantic gestures.

holidays.name: Australia Day
holidays.description: Australia's national day, marked with barbecues, fireworks, citizenship ceremonies, and the beloved tradition of the Australia Day lamington. It is also a day of reflection, protest, and debate, known by many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as Survival Day or Invasion Day.
holidays.origin: Commemorates the 1788 arrival of the First Fleet of British ships at Sydney Cove and the raising of the British flag. It became a national public holiday in all states and territories in 1994.
holidays.funFact: Each year, Australians celebrate with an unofficial tradition of the 'Hottest 100' countdown on the radio station Triple J, which is one of the world's largest annual music polls.

holidays.name: Republic Day (India)
holidays.description: A grand national holiday in India featuring a massive parade in New Delhi with military marches, elaborate cultural floats, camel contingents, and flypasts.
holidays.origin: Marks the day in 1950 when the Constitution of India came into effect, replacing the Government of India Act 1935 and making India a sovereign republic.
holidays.funFact: The celebrations end with the 'Beating Retreat' ceremony, and each year a different world leader is invited as the chief guest of honor.

holidays.name: Letter to an Elder Day
holidays.description: A sweet observance encouraging people to write a heartfelt handwritten letter to an older person in their life, which is a rare treat in the age of text messages.
holidays.origin: A lesser-known awareness observance promoted by community and senior-care groups to fight loneliness among older adults and revive the lost art of letter writing.
holidays.funFact: Many older adults say a physical letter is something they keep and re-read for years, making it a gift that outlasts any emoji.
